newsitem.title: UK: BCCI liquidators to appeal Luxembourg fees ruling.
newsitem.headline: BCCI liquidators to appeal Luxembourg fees ruling.

text.p: Accounting firm Deloitte & Touche said Friday it would appeal a Luxembourg court ruling limiting the fees owed to the firm for its liquidation of collapsed Bank of Credit and Commerce International.

The Luxembourg court fixed Deloitte's fees at 1.8 million pounds ($3.1 million), compared with a request of 2.8 million ($4.9 million) by the firm to cover the first six months of the liquidation process.

Deloitte's managing partner John Connolly described the court ruling as "incomprehensible" -- given that over $4.0 billion of BCCI's $10.0 billion of liabilities had been recovered since it began in 1991.
"The judgment is unacceptable and we will be lodging an appeal against it," Connolly said, adding that Deloitte's rates were well within industry standards and had been approved by British courts.
A total of $218.7 million in fees has been paid to the liquidators of BCCI, a report prepared by them for the British Government revealed in June.
The liquidators were paid $15.1 million in the fifth year of the liquidation ended Jan. 15, 1997, compared to $16 million the previous year.
Fees paid to the liquidator have decreased markedly in recent years as the emphasis of the liquidation has shifted more towards litigation rather than the initial investigation.
BCCI collapsed in 1991 with debts of more than $12 billion and has become the biggest fraud in banking history and the most complex liquidation ever undertaken.
The liquidation looks set to go on for years with major outstanding claims against the auditors of BCCI, Price Waterhouse and Ernst & Young and the Bank of England still to be resolved.
Creditors have already received a 24.5 percent dividend which amounted to over $2 billion and the liquidators expect a further 10 percent will be paid by the end of the year or early in 1998.
